# 314. Example Work Package
## Example Reference: P13-WP07 — Transaction Journal

**Objective**

Ensure multi-file changes can recover after partial execution.

**Read First**

```text
Doc 04 Edit Engine

Doc 10 P13 gates

03_TOOLS_EDITING_EXTRACTION.md
```

**Dependencies**

```text
ChangeSet

file preconditions

Git worktree
```

**Implementation**

1. Define ChangeSet transaction states.
2. Persist journal before writes.
3. Record each file application.
4. Persist pre-image/hash.
5. Mark validation state.
6. Mark committed state.
7. Detect unfinished journal on daemon startup.
8. Add reconciliation function.
9. Add rollback path.
10. Expose transaction evidence.

**Tests**

```text
normal 3-file apply

failure file 2

daemon kill after file 1

external mutation before recovery

successful rollback
```

**Completion**

Pass Doc 10:

```text
P13-G4

P13-G5

P13-G6
```

This is the expected level of specificity for actual development tasks.

---

# 315. Example Work Package
## Example Reference: P12-WP07 — Task Leases

**Objective**

Ensure dead Workers do not permanently own tasks.

**Implementation**

1. Add lease table/fields.
2. Define lease acquisition transaction.
3. Ensure only READY task can acquire lease.
4. Store Worker identity.
5. Store expiry timestamp.
6. Implement heartbeat extension.
7. Implement lease expiry scanner.
8. Transition expired Worker appropriately.
9. Requeue task where safe.
10. Emit events.
11. Add metrics.

**Tests**

```text
normal heartbeat

miss one heartbeat

Worker dies

two Workers race for lease

daemon restart with expired lease
```

**Expected**

Exactly one Worker owns task at any time.

---

# 316. Example Work Package
## Example Reference: P11-WP08 — Context Deduplication

**Objective**

Prevent identical source from appearing repeatedly through multiple retrieval channels.

**Procedure**

1. Define fragment identity.
2. Normalize file/range identifiers.
3. Detect overlapping fragments.
4. Prefer highest-value representation.
5. Convert lower-value duplicate to reference.
6. Recalculate tokens.
7. Preserve retrieval reasons in provenance.
8. Benchmark.

**Tests**

Retrieve same function through:

```text
repo map

symbol lookup

runtime error

semantic search
```

Expected:

```text
one code copy

multiple provenance reasons
```

---

# 317. Example Work Package
## Example Reference: P14-WP13 — Final Audit

**Objective**

Ensure final repository satisfies original mission.

**Procedure**

1. Load immutable original goal.
2. Load requirement matrix.
3. Load integration HEAD.
4. Load latest valid evidence.
5. Load security state.
6. Build independent audit context.
7. Select verifier with diversity preference.
8. Ask verifier to search specifically for omissions.
9. Require structured PASS/FAIL per requirement.
10. Validate claims against deterministic evidence.
11. If failure:
    - create repair task;
    - return mission to repair.
12. If pass:
    - send result to Kernel completion gate.

---

# 318. End-to-End Development Philosophy

Every layer of AgentCode should be built using the same philosophy AgentCode will eventually use itself:

```text
plan

target

implement

observe

verify

record

continue
```

The project should gradually transition from:

```text
human/other coding agents building AgentCode
```

to:

```text
AgentCode building AgentCode.
```

That transition should happen only after the underlying system is trustworthy enough to avoid hiding unfinished work.

---

# 319. When AgentCode May Begin Partial Dogfooding

Partial dogfooding may begin after roughly:

```text
Phase 14
```

when:

```text
Worker

Git/worktrees

Code Intelligence

Context

Autonomy

Edit Engine

Verification
```

are sufficiently operational.

Earlier experimental self-use is allowed.

It must not be treated as proof.

---

# 320. When AgentCode May Become Primary Implementation Agent

Only after Phase 25 repeatedly proves:

```text
useful real self-modification

recovery

verification

low babysitting
```

should AgentCode become the default agent for its own future development.

---

# 321. When a Phase Must Be Reopened

A completed phase must return to:

```text
IMPLEMENTING
```

or:

```text
VALIDATING
```

if later changes break one of its hard gates.

Example:

```text
Phase 13 complete

later Git refactor breaks ChangeSet rollback

→ Phase 13 acceptance becomes stale
```

The roadmap is not write-once history.

---

# 322. When an Acceptance Test Must Be Re-Run

Re-run when:

```text
implementation changes

shared dependency changes

provider interface changes

DB schema changes

sandbox changes

major tool version changes

fixture ground truth changes
```

Use impact analysis rather than rerunning all tests blindly.

---

# 323. Handling Approved Deferrals

A feature may be deferred only when:

```text
not core V1 release-critical
```

and the deferral records:

```text
why

risk

replacement behavior

future phase
```

No silent deferrals.

---

# 324. Definition of "Phase Done"

A phase is done only when:

```text
all required Work Packages accepted

Doc 10 hard gates pass

quality gates pass where applicable

known limitations documented

architecture docs reflect reality

phase completion report exists

next phase has a clean handoff
```

---

# 325. Definition of "Milestone Done"

A milestone is done when its concrete capability operates through AgentCode production architecture and its required tests pass.

Not when:

```text
code compiles.
```

---

# 326. Definition of "Implementation Done"

A feature implementation is done when:

```text
wired

tested

recoverable where required

documented

observable
```

---

# 327. Definition of "Integration Done"

Integration means another real AgentCode subsystem consumes the capability.

Example:

```text
Code Intelligence has repo map API
```

is implementation.

```text
Context Engine actually uses repo map
```

is integration.

---

# 328. Definition of "Verification Done"

Verification means the relevant evidence has been produced and independently challenged when required.

---

# 329. Definition of "Release Done"

Release means:

```text
packaged

installed

smoke tested

documented

legally reviewed

security reviewed

acceptance archived
```

---

---

# 331. Final Implementation Principles

The following principles are mandatory throughout implementation:

1. **Build the runtime before the spectacle.**

2. **Build one reliable Worker before many agents.**

3. **Persist state before relying on autonomy.**

4. **Build repository intelligence before huge-context prompting.**

5. **Build memory with freshness, not eternal summaries.**

6. **Build context retrieval before expensive fanout.**

7. **Build worktree isolation before serious concurrency.**

8. **Build transaction-safe editing before long unattended missions.**

9. **Build verification before trusting completion.**

10. **Build browser execution before trusting frontend claims.**

11. **Build security as reasoning around evidence, not scanner output.**

12. **Build Design Studio around rendered feedback, not one-shot generation.**

13. **Build UI from real Kernel events, not simulated progress.**

14. **Measure cost across verified tasks, not model calls.**

15. **Measure resource use on the real 8 GB target.**

16. **Deliberately break every critical recovery path.**

17. **Use AgentCode on itself before trusting it on others.**

18. **Never allow one LLM conversation to become project truth.**

19. **Never allow one provider to become mission availability.**

20. **Never allow one scanner to become security truth.**

21. **Never allow one Markdown summary to become repository truth.**

22. **Never allow one passing test to become proof of total correctness.**

23. **Never allow a Worker to decide its own completion.**

24. **Never hide a failed hard requirement under "mostly complete."**

25. **Never copy OSS code before understanding license and maintenance cost.**

26. **Never introduce duplicate subsystem authorities.**

27. **Never optimize tokens by removing required evidence.**

28. **Never optimize autonomy by removing safety boundaries.**

29. **Never optimize UI simplicity by hiding important blockers.**

30. **Never call AgentCode V1 complete until Doc 10 says it is.**

---

# 332. Final Statement

This playbook is designed so that implementation can survive changes in:

```text
developer

model

provider

development session

time
```

without losing architectural intent.

A future implementation agent should be able to open the project and determine:

```text
where the project currently is

what the current phase means

what has already been proved

what remains incomplete

what files and extraction reports matter

what tests must be written

what failure behavior must be demonstrated

what may safely be postponed

what absolutely cannot be skipped
```

The project must therefore progress through **small, evidence-backed engineering increments**, not large model-generated code dumps.

At every phase the implementation pattern remains:

```text
UNDERSTAND
    ↓
DECOMPOSE
    ↓
IMPLEMENT
    ↓
WIRE
    ↓
TEST
    ↓
BREAK
    ↓
RECOVER
    ↓
VERIFY
    ↓
DOCUMENT
    ↓
HAND OFF
```

The intended result is that even if the original project designer, current implementation agent, or current model disappears entirely, AgentCode development can continue with the same architectural intent and quality standard.

When this playbook is followed together with Docs 01–10, the project should not depend on institutional memory, chat history or assumptions.

It should depend on:

```text
architecture

structured plans

source code

tests

evidence

acceptance gates

persistent documentation
```

which is exactly the engineering philosophy AgentCode itself is intended to embody.

This document is the **V1 operational implementation source of truth for executing every AgentCode development phase, milestone and work package from architecture freeze through final V1 release.**
